title: Find every candidate worth talking to
description: Use Strawberry across job definition, talent mapping, sourcing, applications, interviews, candidate outreach, and recruiting pipeline review.
introduction: Recruiting gets fragmented quickly. The role lives in a document, candidates are spread across LinkedIn and the ATS, interview evidence sits in notes and transcripts, and the reason behind a decision is often still in someone's head.

Strawberry can work across the visible browser, logged-in sourcing tools, the ATS, meetings, documents, and the other places that hold the hiring context. A job definition can stay connected to the search, the search to the interviews, and the interview evidence to the pipeline decision. As the team corrects the work, the companion can remember the hiring bar and the sources it trusts.

sections.title: What Strawberry can help you do

items.title: Define the role and search
items.description: Turn the hiring need into honest criteria, a clear job description, and a realistic talent market.

items.title: Find and review candidates
items.description: Build a calibrated candidate set and review inbound applications against the same evidence bar.

items.title: Prepare interviews and synthesize feedback
items.description: Decide what each interviewer should learn, then bring the evidence back to the criteria.

items.title: Communicate with candidates
items.description: Draft relevant outreach and follow-up with the relationship and prior contact in view.

items.title: Review the recruiting pipeline
items.description: See bottlenecks, ownership, candidate experience, and whether the current mix can support the goal.

blocks.text: Not sure where to begin? Your companion can look at the role and hiring work you have open and suggest a useful skill to try first.

skill.context: Choose and complete the recruiting workflow that would help this role most now.

blocks.text: A good search starts by separating the internal hiring need from the candidate-facing job description. Strawberry can use the plan, org context, role history, manager input, and current market evidence to make the criteria explicit, write the role honestly, and test whether the expected titles, backgrounds, location, and compensation make sense.

items.title: Define the job
items.text: Clarify the outcomes, responsibilities, evidence of success, constraints, and honest candidate-facing description.

skill.context: Define the internal role and create an honest candidate-facing job description.

items.title: Map the talent market
items.text: Check the titles, employers, adjacent backgrounds, geography, compensation, and likely supply before scaling the search.

skill.context: Clarify titles, employers, adjacent backgrounds, geography, compensation, and supply.

blocks.text: Sourced candidates and inbound applicants arrive differently, but both need job-related criteria, visible evidence, clear uncertainty, and a human decision. Strawberry can work through the relevant profiles, applications, ATS history, and prior contact, explain why someone may fit, and keep what still needs checking visible.

items.title: Build the candidate set
items.text: Review a varied sample first, correct the search, and then complete the set at the scale the role needs.

skill.context: Build an evidence-backed candidate set and refine the search before scaling.

items.title: Review inbound applications
items.text: Apply the same accepted criteria to the application set while preserving evidence, uncertainty, and the human decision.

skill.context: Review an application set against the accepted role criteria.

sections.title: Carry the same hiring bar through interviews

blocks.text: Interview preparation works best when each person knows what evidence they own and what the team still needs to learn. Strawberry can turn the role and earlier candidate evidence into a structured plan, useful questions, probes, and scorecards.

Afterward, the transcript and panel feedback can be mapped back to the same criteria. Contradictions, candidate claims, interviewer judgments, and unknowns stay visible instead of disappearing into one confident score.

items.title: Prepare the evidence plan
items.text: Give each interviewer a clear area to test, useful questions and probes, and the context they need about the candidate.

skill.context: Prepare the interview plan, candidate and panel briefs, questions, probes, and scorecards.

items.title: Bring the evidence back together
items.text: Map transcripts and panel feedback to the criteria while keeping contradictions, judgments, and unknowns visible.

skill.context: Turn transcripts and feedback into an evidence-backed draft assessment for human review.

blocks.text: Candidate outreach has a different relationship from sales outreach. Strawberry can use the role, professional context, prior contact, and the team's employer story to draft a message that explains why the conversation may be worth having. It can also prepare thoughtful follow-up without turning a candidate list into an automatic sequence.

items.context: Prepare candidate-aware messages and review the exact send before it happens.

sections.title: See whether the pipeline can support the goal

blocks.text: A recruiting pipeline review should show what needs attention now and whether the current candidate mix can plausibly support the hiring goal. Your companion can connect ATS state with sourcing, applications, correspondence, interviews, and calendars while keeping proposed corrections separate.

If coverage looks weak, the next step may be reviewing an inbound backlog, sourcing more candidates, or revisiting the talent market. A review recommends the best handoff without launching a large search automatically.

items.context: Review priorities, candidate experience, evidence gaps, ATS corrections, and pipeline coverage.

blocks.text: Once one workflow works, preserve the accepted criteria, sources, fields, and review points so the next role does not begin from a generic template. Share the result, the method, or the wider Recruiting companion only when that level of context is actually useful. Add a Routine after the process and ownership have settled.
